Triage: lands in `.github/workflows/release.yml` (+ release tooling under `scripts/`); rationale: `domain:devx` (workflow/gate face). → `pm:queue`, Bug — the repo's own `lint.yml:1249` comment already concedes the version PR merges with no CI; premise re-verified on `origin/main` (the version-PR step still runs `changesets/action@v1` with the default `GITHUB_TOKEN`, and the deliberate absence of a `publish:` input per #6170 is an invariant to preserve, not part of the defect). Scope notes for dispatch: (a) objectui's fix (objectui#5397 / PR objectui#6217) is a sweep of the same defect, not a portable patch — the two version lanes have diverged; (b) cloud/objectos halves: one grep for `changesets/action` + the token it is handed, then file at destination — objectos has no changeset flow per its lane charter, so verify before filing rather than porting blind. Size/model suggestion: M, opus.

## ⛔ Release-adjacent WORK, not a release ACT — the distinction is the whole reason this is dispatchable

AGENTS.md Prime Directive #15 reserves the **release act**: ⛔ `changeset publish` / `pnpm run release`, ⛔ pushing a version tag, ⛔ cutting a GitHub Release, ⛔ pushing a runtime image, ⛔ `workflow_dispatch`-ing `release.yml`, ⛔ **approving a pending `release` environment deployment**, and ⛔ merging — or queueing, or arming auto-merge on — the **Version Packages** PR.

**Editing `release.yml` to add a validation step is none of those.** The directive says release-adjacent work stays open to every seat. But the dev must not cross into the reserved list while working in that file, and in particular ⛔ must never touch the standing `chore: version packages` PR.

## What is already ruled, and what is explicitly NOT inherited

The maintainer ruled **option A** on the sibling (objectui#5397, 2026-08-22, 「接受所有」): validate the post-version tree **inside the release workflow**, after the version step and before `changesets/action` opens or updates the PR. A PAT / GitHub App token was **rejected** (widens the supply-chain trust surface, adds rotation obligations); per-artifact guarantees were **rejected** (they do not generalise).

⚠️ **The scope conclusion does NOT transfer, and this is the trap.** In objectui the price chose the implementation, and the naive reading was wrong: `changeset version` there moves **no source byte at all**, so a full post-version suite would re-test what CI validated minutes earlier. But `pnpm run version` **here** is `changeset version` + `sync-protocol-version` + `sync-template-versions` (+ `sync-docs-image-tags`) — a strictly larger post-version diff. **Measure this repo's own, and let that choose the shape.** Copying objectui's ~68s surface list would be inheriting a number that was derived from a different workflow.

Triage adds two constraints I am carrying as binding: the deliberate absence of a `publish:` input (per #6170) is **an invariant to preserve, not part of the defect**; and for the cloud/objectos halves — one grep for `changesets/action` and the token it is handed, then **file at destination**, ⛔ never port blind, because objectos has no changeset flow per its lane charter.

The cost of leaving this is on the record: #9064 exists because a gate structurally could not fire on the release PR, so a per-artifact rewriter had to be built for one artifact. `sync-template-versions.mjs` and `sync-protocol-version` are two more of the same kind — each new version-time output needs its own rewriter and self-test **forever**, because nothing validates the tree as a whole.

Tier: **opus** — triage suggested it and I agree. Derived live, no path-derived mandate, so sonnet is the floor and this is a judgment call: the shape follows from a measurement nobody has taken yet, and the failure mode is a validation step that looks thorough while covering the wrong surface.
